problems.problem: The reading inverts Rashi’s logic in its syntax: in ‘a law that, like all the Torah, was fit to come through Moses, since merit is brought about by the meritorious’ the ‘since’ clause attaches to ‘fit to come through Moses’, so it reads as if Moses’ merit were the reason. In Rashi on 9:7 the section should have been said by Moses like the rest of the Torah, but these men merited that it be said through them, because merit is brought about through the worthy (שֶׁמְּגַלְגְּלִין זְכוּת עַ"יְ זַכַּאי).
problems.fix: Unclean from a corpse at Passover, some men come before Moses and Aaron; Rashi, on 9:7, reads the law their plea wins as one fit to come through Moses like all the Torah, given through them since merit is brought about by the meritorious. (44 words; same evidence, Rashi on 9:7)
